necessity.text: The one-shot local Python check is justified because emitall checks declarative receipt claims but does not by itself bind file-manifest payloads together with literal line-range quotations. Standard pathlib, json and hashlib operations suffice; no reusable scientific instrument is added. Failure means a wrong pin, path, byte count, quotation, duplicate path, receipt unit or expected count. Before reading real manifests, the same row comparator must accept a synthetic clean row and reject corrupted bytes, a corrupted hash and a corrupted size. An exact-quotation comparator must accept its clean fixture and reject an altered quotation. These are document-check controls and confer no mathematical independence.
